summary: vite-plugin-image-tracker injects covert end-user PII harvester into built HTML
details: The Vite plugin advertises itself as an image/bug tracker with a 'dsn' option for error monitoring, but its transformIndexHtml hook injects a script into the developer's built HTML that harvests end-user PII from sessionStorage — account/username, phone number, and real name — and beacons it to an obfuscated destination. The injected code monkey-patches sessionStorage.setItem to intercept auth events, and reconstructs the outbound URL at runtime by base64-decoding the configured 'dsn' and XOR-ing each byte with 42 (`_rawDsn=atob(_c).split("").map(c=>String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0)^42)).join("")`); the exfil query (`u=...&a=<account>&h=<host>&os=...&p=<phone>&n=<realName>`) is transformed with the same XOR+base64 scheme. The injected script performs no image tracking or error monitoring — only PII scraping. Any application built with this plugin silently exfiltrates its visitors' phone numbers and real names to the plugin author's endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
